toolChoice.fallbackUsed: god-tibo-imagen (gti) for one seamless-tileable color 'hero' texture per theme, THEN deterministic per-frame assembly in a new script (tools/gen_terrain_fx_sheets.py) instead of asking gti to draw the whole NxN grid directly in one shot. Rationale: asking a single image-gen call to lay out a clean, evenly-aligned animated grid is unreliable — the existing character-asset-pipeline already rejected a generated atlas for drawing bogus section labels onto the sheet (docs/character-asset-pipeline.md:99, 'v2 was rejected as a reference candidate after visual review found generated section labels'). Deterministic assembly guarantees exact 4x4 alignment and a mathematically seamless loop (phase in [0, 2*pi) wraps exactly at frame 0 == frame N). A color prompt ('seamless tileable game texture, molten volcanic basalt...') still reads much better to the image model than an abstract grayscale-pattern prompt would, so the hero stays color and is reduced to a pattern mask in code afterward (see grayscaleConversion below).

grayscaleConversion.requirement: vfx-lane consumer contract (2026-08-07): grayscale/alpha pattern only, no color — runtime applies per-stage tint (lava=emissive pattern, ice=crystal-drift pattern, shift=drifting-ash pattern).
grayscaleConversion.method: load_pattern_base() in tools/gen_terrain_fx_sheets.py: per-pixel max(R,G,B) of the color hero texture, then min-max contrast stretch to the full 0-255 range. max(R,G,B) was chosen over standard luminance (0.299R+0.587G+0.114B) because luminance under-weights the blue channel (0.114), which would wash out the ice/shift themes' cyan glow elements relative to lava's orange ones — max-channel isolates 'how bright is the brightest color component here' uniformly regardless of hue, which is what actually reads as 'glowing/bright element vs dark base' across all 3 themes.
grayscaleConversion.qualityCheck: Visually reviewed all 3 finished sheets after conversion (Read tool image preview) before shipping: lava shows crack lines as bright strands against a near-black base, ice shows crystal texture + a clearly visible sweeping diagonal glint band, shift shows the ash/current texture + clearly visible vertical drift bands. All read as usable pattern masks; no regeneration of the hero textures was needed.

perThemeTransform.lava: Pulsing glow brightness (sine phase over the 16 frames, boosts only already-bright/'hot' texels above a grayscale threshold) + partial vertical roll of the base pattern (bubbling-flow read). frame_lava() in the script, grayscale (numpy) throughout.
perThemeTransform.ice: Diagonal glint band sweeps across the tile once per loop, drawn 3x (current + one cycle earlier/later) so the wrap has no visible gap, Gaussian-blurred, added on top of the base pattern (clipped to 255). frame_ice().
perThemeTransform.shift: Horizontal drift band rolls across the tile (position = phase * width, wrapped modulo width), Gaussian-blurred, added on top of the base pattern. frame_shift().

gridSpec.grid: 4x4 (16 frames) — chosen over 8x8 per D8/W16's own '4x4 or 8x8' allowance; 16 frames is enough for a smooth ambient loop at typical ~8-12 fps flipbook playback and keeps each frame at a readable 256px
gridSpec.sheetSize: 1024x1024 px (<=1024 WebGL ceiling, CLAUDE.md §1 — verified via PIL after generation, no resize needed since GRID*FRAME_SIZE=1024 by construction)
gridSpec.frameOrder: row-major, frame 0 = top-left cell, frame index = row*4 + col, reading left-to-right then top-to-bottom
gridSpec.loop: Seamless: every per-theme transform is parameterized by phase = frame_index / 16 (or 2*pi*frame_index/16 for the sine-based lava pulse), so frame 15 -> frame 0 continues the cycle exactly as frame N -> frame N+1 would inside it. No dedicated 'frame 16' duplicate of frame 0 is included — playback should loop directly from index 15 back to index 0.
gridSpec.pixelFormat: 8-bit grayscale (PNG mode L), no alpha channel, no color — matches the confirmed contract exactly.

findings: cinder-span ("재의 다리"): 'weathered charcoal basalt block masonry veined with dull orange ember cracks' / 'scorched stone bridge decking' -> matches terrain-fx-lava-sheet directly. This is the stage with EmberGalleryHazards (vent hazards) too.

echo-throne ("메아리 왕좌"): 'regal dark blue granite throne-hall masonry with silver-blue veining' / 'mirror-dark throne floor tiles with concentric pale blue echo rings' -> matches terrain-fx-ice-sheet directly. This is also the stage carrying HazardConfig.Current(...) (StageCatalog.cs:147), i.e. the existing TideCurrent hazard kind.
abyss-chancel ("서약의 성당"): violet-grey/indigo cathedral palette — neither lava nor ice; not targeted by this sheet set.

No stage in StageCatalog.cs is literally named 'volcano' or 'glacier' — cinder-span/echo-throne are this repo's closest thematic matches and are what the lava/ice hero textures were originally prompted against (the color source, before grayscale reduction, explicitly says 'cinder-span stage palette' / 'echo-throne stage palette' — the pattern geometry survives grayscale conversion even though the hue does not).

terrain-fx-shift-sheet is intentionally generic (not stage-locked): it targets HazardKind.TideCurrent (Assets/Scripts/View/EnvironmentBuilder.cs:809, VfxDirector.cs:128/142/1248/1445), which StageCatalog.cs uses on echo-throne (HazardConfig.Current(768f,604f,120f,0.3f) at :147) and the ash-verdict-adjacent anchor (:485) — i.e. 'moving terrain' maps to the existing current/tide hazard visual, not a new stage.
